svg.title: Supervision and Recordkeeping Cadence
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-07-supervision-cadence; chapter number: 4; title: Supervision and Recordkeeping Cadence; subtitle: Inspection cycles and record buckets in years; caption: OSJs are inspected annually, while branches run on three-year cycles. Records sit in six-year and three-year buckets, with two years kept easily accessible.; assumptions note: Year counts are the practitioner-cited cycles and record buckets. Rule 1017 separately triggers at 25% of assets or ownership control, filed at least 30 days before the change.; note: Sources are The Finance Lab on OSJ inspections and Rule 1017, and Business Broker Crowd Call on licensing context.; chart type: stacked_comparison; total range: 1 to 6 years; buckets: label: OSJ Inspection Cycle; low: 1; high: 1; notes: Mandatory annual inspections once a branch manager gives final new-account approval; label: Branch Inspection Cycle; low: 3; high: 3; notes: Three-year cycle for non-OSJ branches; label: Long Record Bucket; low: 6; high: 6; notes: Six-year retention bucket, first two years easily accessible; label: Short Record Bucket; low: 3; high: 3; notes: Three-year retention bucket, first two years easily accessible
